Issue #2673 -- command-line -D defines are duplicated on the way to the preprocessor.

Scroll the output to the metadata at the end and compare two nodes against the
CHECK lines in the source above (this file is DXC's own test, unmodified):

  !dx.source.defines -> !N = !{!"DefineA=1", !"DefineB=0", !"DefineA=1", !"DefineB=0"}
       two -D flags were passed; each is recorded twice. The test's own
       "// CHECK: !{!"DefineA=1", !"DefineB=0"}" expects one of each.

  !dx.source.args    -> the pair !"-D", !"DefineA", !"-D", !"DefineB=0" appears
       once where it was typed and a second time after !"-Qstrip_reflect":
       the driver re-appends the defines it already parsed out of the argv.
       (Ignore the repeated !"-Zi" and the !"-Qembed_debug" -- those are added
       by Compiler Explorer's own wrapper, not by this bug.)

The compile succeeds and the DXIL is correct -- only the recorded defines are
wrong. Both DXC panes show it, and it is the same on every release from
v1.4.1907 (2019) to v1.9.2607.
